nodes.name: Cu-Foam Cleaning and Cu(OH)₂ Nanoarrays
nodes.procedure: Cu-Foam (1×1 cm²) was cleaned up with 0.01 M HCl for 24 h. A piece of Cu-Foam was rinsed with deionized (DI) water, and then put into the mixture solution of (NH₄)₂S₂O₈ (10 mL × 0.2 M) and NaOH (10 mL × 5 M) for 60 min at 25°C. Then, the sample was cleaned with deionized water and dried at 50°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: CuCo-LDH Nanosheet Arrays
nodes.procedure: The mixed solution of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (20 mL × 0.1 M) and CH₄N₂O (10 mL × 0.2 M) was transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. Then, the as-prepared Cu(OH)₂ was put into the autoclave and kept at 130°C for 8 h. The sample was taken out, cooled to room temperature, cleaned with deionized water (DI), and dried at 50°C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of CuCo-LDH Nanosheet Arrays: The mixed solution of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O... dried at 50°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: CuCo-LDH Activation
nodes.procedure: The CuCo-LDH was activated via a CV method with the voltage window of 0 - 0.6 V at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ in 3 M KOH until the curve was stable, which could produce a large number of hydrogen vacancies.
nodes.source_text: First, the CuCo-LDH was activated via a CV method with the voltage window of 0 - 0.6 V... until the curve was stable

nodes.name: Zn²⁺ Intercalation
nodes.procedure: The preparation of CuCo-LDH/Zn²⁺ was realized by a CV method with the voltage window of -0.75 - 0 V at scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ in Zn(NO₃)₂·6H₂O solution of 0.5 M until the curve was stable, which can enable zinc ion intercalation.
nodes.source_text: Then, the preparation of CuCo-LDH/Zn²⁺ was realized by a CV method... in Zn(NO₃)₂·6H₂O solution of different concentrations (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 M) until the curve was stable

nodes.name: CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs and CuCo-LDH-S
nodes.procedure: Finally, the CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs was prepared in TAA solution (20 mL × 0.015 M) at 120°C for 2 h. In addition, the CuCo-LDH-S was prepared by the same hydrothermal method at 120°C.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: prepared in TAA solution (20 mL × 0.015 M) at 120°C for 2 h

nodes.source_text: Finally, the CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs was prepared in TAA solution (20 mL × 0.015 mm) at 100, 120, and 140°C for 2 h. In addition, the CuCo-LDH-S was prepared by the same hydrothermal method at 120°C.

nodes.description: Three-electrode supercapacitor testing - comparative capacitance at 2 mA cm⁻² and 20 mV s⁻¹
nodes.source_text: In Figure S13 ... CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs reflect the maximum area of closed CV curve and discharge times, showing the highest area specific capacitance (Ca) of 7.82 F cm⁻² ... According to the GCD curves (Figure 4b), the Ca of CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs is 7.45, 7.82, 7.49, 5.61, 5.14, and 4.43 F cm⁻² at 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, and 20 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: Hybrid supercapacitor device performance with AC anode in 3 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the as-assembled hybrid supercapacitors display an outstanding energy density of 299 μWh cm⁻² at power density of 1600 μW cm⁻², with outstanding capacitance retention of 102.3% and coulomb efficiency of 96.2% after 10 000 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images confirm CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs retains stable 3D self-supporting nanosheet array morphology identical to CuCo-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Observed from SEM images, the morphology and nanostructure of CuCo-LDH-S (Figure S2, Supporting Information) and CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs have not changed as compared to CuCo-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS reveals Cu, Co, O in CuCo-LDH; confirms Cu, Co, O, S, Zn in CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs with optimal Zn content 5.25 wt% (SEM-EDS, Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The relevant energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS, Figure S1, Supporting Information) reveals the existence of Cu, Co, and O... optimum amount of Zn element is 5.25% in CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs based on Scanning Electron Microscopy-Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (SEM-EDS, Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows (003), (009), (012) planes of CuCo-LDH preserved in CuCo-LDH-S; interlayer spacing expands from 6.2 Å to 6.5 Å with Zn²⁺ and 6.7 Å with ZnS-QDs; new ZnS (201), (331) peaks appear.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of these electrode material are shown in Figure 2b. The peaks indexed to the (003), (009), and (012) planes... two new characteristic peaks appeared that correspond to the (201) and (331) planes of ZnS phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Cu²⁺ (Cu 2p₃/₂ 934.7 eV, 2p₁/₂ 954.6 eV), Co²⁺/Co³⁺ (Co 2p 780.6-797.8 eV), Zn 2p shift to lower binding energy forming Zn-S bonds, O-vacancy (O 1s 531.7 eV), S 2p (162.3/163.5 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2c, the two peaks at 954.6 and 934.7 eV correspond to Cu 2p₁/₂ and Cu 2p₃/₂... S replaced part of the O on the laminate to form abundant oxygen vacancies (O-vacancy, 531.7 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals smooth CuCo-LDH nanosheets, stable 2D structure in CuCo-LDH-S, interlayer ZnS-QDs (3-5 nm diameter) in broken layers of CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the magnified TEM images (Figure 3e), it can be observed that the diameter of interlaminar ZnS-QDs is ≈ 3 - 5 nm... interlayer QDs can be clearly found in the broken outer layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows CuCo-LDH lattice fringes 1.5 Å (111), 2.4 Å (009); CuCo-LDH-S has curved morphology with lattice defects; ZnS-QDs show 1.2 Å (311), 1.6 Å (211) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As described in the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), the obvious lattice fringes with the spacings of 1.5 and 2.4 Å reflect the (111) and (009) plane... interplanar distances of 1.2 and 1.6 Å reflect the (311) and (211) planes of the ZnS phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs has minimum solution resistance Rs = 0.6905 Ω and charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.2821 Ω; lowest ion diffusion resistance σ = 0.76 Ω s⁻¹/².
nodes.evidence_snippet: CuCo-LDH-S/ZnS-QDs has the minimum internal resistance of solution (Rs = 0.6905 Ω)... lower interface charge transfer resistance (Rct = 0.2821)... smallest σ of 0.76 Ω s⁻¹/².
